pack.title: Pack PFS image
pack.subtitle: Create .ffpfsc / .ffpfs / .exfat images from a game folder or file (backend: MkPFS).
pack.hint.folder: Default and most compatible layout: the folder is wrapped in exFAT and compressed in a single pass.
pack.hint.raw: Packs the folder straight into PFS. With compression enabled the console may read files incorrectly — use only if you know why.
pack.hint.file: Converts an existing .exfat or .ffpkg image into a compressed .ffpfsc.
pack.hint.exfat: Builds an uncompressed exFAT image from the folder.
fpkg.title: Build FPKG
fpkg.subtitle: Build a PS5 .pkg from a game folder, exFAT image or GP5 project (backend: fpkg-cli + Sony Publishing Tools).
fpkg.info.title: Title
fpkg.warn.noParam: sce_sys/param.json not found in the selected folder.
fpkg.warn.keystone: sce_sys/keystone (exactly 96 bytes) is missing — the Sony SDK build needs it. Add it or enable “Built-in engine”.
fpkg.cleanJunk: Remove junk files (.DS_Store, Thumbs.db) from source
fpkg.noSonySdk: Built-in engine (do not use Sony SDK)
tools.title: Inspect & extract
tools.subtitle: Info, listing, verification and extraction for .pkg packages and PFS / exFAT images.
settings.title: Settings
settings.subtitle: Interface and bundled tools. All settings are stored next to the program (PS5CombineAIO.ini).
settings.toolsHint: The program calls these tools from the tools folder next to it, so it runs on any PC without installation.
about.title: About
about.subtitle: Authors, sources and license.
about.desc: All-in-one PS5 toolkit: PFS images, FPKG building, inspection and extraction in a single portable application.
about.authorRole: idea, combined C++/Qt application, interface, build scripts.
about.psvRole: Cross-platform FPKG builder application and fpkg-cli.
about.drakRole: Author of LibProsperoPkg — the FPKG core (PFS v2/v3, Kraken, PlayGo, verification).
about.sonyRole: Proprietary, not covered by this program's license; not part of the source code.
about.license: This program is distributed under GNU GPL v3 (required by MkPFS, which is GPL-3.0). Third-party components keep their own licenses.
about.notice: Intended for homebrew and development on debug-enabled consoles. Use responsibly and respect the licenses of the tools you bundle.

Stop it and exit?

lib.title: Library
lib.subtitle: Dumps, .pkg packages and images from your folders — with search, filters, cover and firmware check.
lib.noFolders: Add a folder with dumps, .pkg, .ffpfsc, .ffpkg or .exfat files, then press Rescan.
lib.removePrompt: Folder to remove from the library:
lib.search: Search: title, ID, file name… (use -word to exclude)
lib.col.title: Title
lib.fw.tooHigh: Requires firmware %1, your console has %2 — the game will not start unless the requirement is lowered.
lib.fw.ok: By param.json and SDK the game fits firmware %1.
lib.fw.noConsole: Set your console firmware in Settings to check compatibility.
settings.consoleFwHint: Console firmware flags games that need a newer one (for example 7.61). The second field is the upper limit of your loader/exploit (for example “up to 11.60” from the release notes): it is not stored in the game files, so it is entered manually. Empty = check disabled.
pack.root.found:

A game root was found inside:
%1

Use it instead?
pack.root.missing:
The selected folder has no: %1

An image made from it will most likely NOT start on the console. You probably selected the wrong folder level.

Pack anyway?
fpkg.imageNote: Image selected: its contents are read during the build (extracted to a temporary folder, removed automatically afterwards).
fpkg.compatHint: By default the builder lowers the required firmware to the game's SDK version when it is higher. This only changes the package metadata: a game that uses newer system features can still crash on an older firmware. The options below work with the built-in engine only.
fpkg.keepFw: Do not lower the required firmware (--keep-required-fw)
fpkg.engineAsk:
The options %1 work only with the built-in engine — the Sony SDK ignores them.

Switch to the built-in engine?
hint.retail: This looks like a retail package, not a debug (FPKG) one. The tool only reads debug packages; retail packages cannot be decoded without the image keys.
hint.keystone: A 96-byte sce_sys\keystone is required for the Sony SDK build. Add it or enable the built-in engine.
hint.paramJson: Check that sce_sys\param.json exists in the root of the selected folder.
hint.locked: A file is in use by another program (antivirus, Explorer, another tool). Close it and retry.
hint.access: Access denied: pick a folder you can write to or run the program as administrator.
hint.disk: Not enough free disk space for the output or the temporary folder.
about.pkgtoolRole: Reference for the library manager and firmware-version format.
job.queuedRestored: Queued tasks: %1 (open “Tasks” and press Start queue)
tasks.title: Tasks
tasks.subtitle: The queue of all runs. It is saved between launches: a task interrupted by closing the program comes back as “Interrupted” and can be retried.
lib.helperMissing: Trophies, activities and files inside images need ps5aio-helper (tools\ps5aio). Put PS5PKGTool-1.2.0 into third_party and rebuild.
lib.detailsErrors: Some sections could not be read: %1

lib.uds.col.name: Name

lib.files.selectFirst: Select one or more files first.
tools.maintHint: Works on the file selected above; the format (exFAT / FFPKG / FFPFSC) is detected from its contents. Verify: all three. Repair and AMPR refresh: exFAT only. Edit files: exFAT and FFPKG. Rebuild: FFPKG. FFPFSC can only be verified, converted or extracted. Changes are made in place (with a verified swap) — keep a copy.
tools.needHelper: This function needs ps5aio-helper (tools\ps5aio). Put PS5PKGTool-1.2.0 into third_party and rebuild.
tools.confirmInPlace:
The image will be modified in place. Make sure you have a copy.

Continue?
edit.title: Edit files in image (exFAT / FFPKG)
edit.hint: Build a list of changes. They are applied together on a staging copy, verified, and only then swapped in.
edit.askImagePath: Path inside the image (use /, for example sce_sys/param.json):
lib.fw.aboveLoader: Console firmware %1 is above the limit of your loader (%2) — the game will not start.
lib.fw.needsAboveLoader: The game needs firmware %1, which is above the limit of your loader (%2).
dup.title: Duplicates
dup.none: No duplicates found: nothing has the same Content ID and version.
dup.summary: Duplicate sets: %1 · extra copies: %2 · space: %3. Nothing is deleted automatically — tick the copies to remove; they go to the Recycle Bin.
dup.allMarked: All copies of one item are ticked. Leave at least one.
dup.confirm: Move %1 item(s) (%2) to the Recycle Bin?
ren.title: Rename by template
ren.hint: Applies to the items currently shown in the list (use the filter first). Tokens: {TITLE} {TITLE_ID} {CONTENT_ID} {VERSION} {CATEGORY} {REGION} {PLATFORM} {FW} {SDK}. Existing names are never overwritten.
ren.confirm: Rename %1 item(s)? Paths in saved tasks that point to them will stop working.
cmp.needTwo: Comparison needs at least two items in the Library: add the folder with our image and the known-good reference.
cmp.title: Image comparison
cmp.hint: Pick our image (A) and a known-good reference (B) — both must be in the Library. The file set, sizes, param.json fields and the eboot.bin location are compared. File contents are compared byte by byte: always for files up to 16 MB, larger ones only with the checkbox below.
cmp.deep: Compare all files byte by byte (slow: both images are read in full)
cmp.deepTip: Without it, files larger than 16 MB are compared by size only
cmp.sum.counts: Only in B: %1 · only in A: %2 · different: %3 · identical, verified by content: %4 · identical by size (not compared byte by byte): %5
cmp.sum.notDeep: Only files up to 16 MB were compared byte by byte. Enable the full comparison to check larger files too.
cmp.f.noEbootA: A has no eboot.bin — the game cannot start.
cmp.f.noEbootB: B (reference) has no eboot.bin — make sure you picked the right image.
cmp.f.rootShift: The game root is placed differently: in A eboot.bin is in “%1”, in B it is in “%2”. Paths were aligned for the comparison, but in a working image eboot.bin must sit directly in the root.
cmp.f.onlyB: The reference has files that are missing here: %1 — a likely cause of the crash: they did not make it into the image (see “Missing here”).
cmp.f.onlyA: Extra files here (not in the reference): %1. Usually harmless — see the tab.
cmp.f.diffData: Data files differ: %1. That can be normal between releases and backports; if a file here is much smaller it may not have been copied fully or may be damaged.
cmp.f.diffExe: Executables differ (eboot.bin, .sprx, etc.): %1. Expected if the reference was backported for another firmware or comes from another release.
cmp.f.case: File name letter case differs: %1. Check the case-sensitivity option used when packing.
cmp.f.identical: No differences: file set, sizes and parameters match.
pack.pkgOnly: Package-only files were found in sce_sys: %1. They are merged in when an FPKG is extracted, are not part of the game file system and should not be in an image that is launched as a folder.
pack.pkgOnly.moved:
The files were moved (not deleted) to: %1
Move them back if you need them.
ampr.missing:
The game uses libSceAmpr (found in eboot.bin) but the folder has no emulator fakelib/libSceAmpr.sprx — it is stripped when an FPKG is built. Without it a game launched as an image may crash at start.

Add the AMPR emulator (drakmor/ampr_emu, GPL-3.0) to the source folder? MkPFS will create ampr_emu.index itself.
ampr.pickVersion: AMPR emulator version (different games need different ones):
ampr.label.old: %1 — often for BP and older dumps
ampr.added: AMPR emulator %1 was added as fakelib/libSceAmpr.sprx. If the game does not start, try another version.
ampr.failed: Could not add the AMPR emulator: %1
ampr.noBundled: The ampr_emu modules were not found in tools\ampr_emu — they cannot be added automatically.
pack.rawWarn: “Plain PFS” (--raw) with compression is selected. Such an image can pass verification yet be read incorrectly by the console. The recommended mode is “Folder → .ffpfsc”. Continue?
lib.ampr.ok: AMPR: the game uses libSceAmpr and the emulator is present in fakelib (version %1).
lib.ampr.missing: AMPR: the game uses libSceAmpr but fakelib/libSceAmpr.sprx is missing — launched as an image it may crash at start. The program will offer to add the emulator when packing.
lib.pkgOnly: sce_sys contains package-only files: %1 — they should not be in the image (the program will offer to remove them when packing).
cmp.f.amprMissing: The reference has the AMPR emulator (fakelib/libSceAmpr.sprx) and we do not — a likely cause of the crash at start. The program will offer to add it when packing.
cmp.f.amprIndex: The reference has ampr_emu.index and we do not. MkPFS creates it itself when fakelib/libSceAmpr.sprx is in the folder.
cmp.f.amprDiffer: The AMPR emulator differs from the reference — different games need different versions (0.3.6.6 or 0.4.2.1).
cmp.f.pkgOnly: sce_sys here has package-only files that the reference does not: %1 — an image launched as a folder should not contain them.
settings.amprAuto: Add the AMPR emulator when packing without asking (if the game needs it)
settings.amprHint: If eboot.bin uses libSceAmpr and fakelib/libSceAmpr.sprx is missing from the folder, the program adds the selected ampr_emu build to the source folder before packing. Which version a game needs is not known in advance: if it does not start, pack again with the other one. Without the checkbox the program asks each time.
pack.job.ampr: AMPR index inside the exFAT image
lib.ampr.noEboot: AMPR: eboot.bin was not found in the folder root — cannot check.
lib.ampr.no: AMPR: eboot.bin (%1, %2) does not reference libSceAmpr — the emulator is not required. Modules in fakelib: %3.
settings.amprForce: Always add the AMPR emulator — even if eboot.bin does not mention libSceAmpr (for cases when the check does not trigger)
cmp.f.geometry: The exFAT structure differs: %1. These are image-building parameters, not game data: the reference may have been built by another tool. For plain exFAT you can choose the cluster size on the “PFS packing” page.
pack.clusterTip: Only for the “plain exFAT” mode. “auto” is 64 KiB (the MkPFS default). If a working image has a different cluster size (see “Compare images” → “exFAT structure”), set the same.
backport.title: Game backport
backport.subtitle: Lower the SDK version and fake-sign a game’s executables from a folder, so a dump from newer firmware can run on a console with older firmware (Auto-Backpork backend).
backport.mode.downgrade: Lower SDK and sign only (files already decrypted)
backport.noBackup: Do not create backups when lowering
backport.notice: Next: pack the output folder into an image (“PFS packing” page). The console must run the BackPork payload, which mounts the game’s fakelib. The program does not contain Sony system libraries: take the fakelib folder from your own console or your own games. Use only with games dumped from your console. Pairs 11–13 were added by the program (the Auto-Backpork table ends at 10) and are not verified on a console: if the game does not start, try a neighbouring pair.
backport.infoHint: Pick a game folder: the program will show the required firmware and SDK from param.json.
backport.infoNoParam: This folder has no readable sce_sys/param.json — is it really the game root?
backport.infoConsole: Your console firmware: %1 — the SDK pair is preselected from it.
backport.needTool: Backport needs tools\backpork\backpork-cli.exe. Put the Auto-Backpork-main folder into third_party and rebuild (build.bat).
backport.outInside: The output folder must not be the game folder or lie inside it.
backport.ack: Backport works on game files dumped from your own console. Do not distribute the result or Sony’s system libraries. Continue?
backport.noFakelib: No fakelib folder is set. Without the system libraries a backport usually will not start on the console (take them from your own console or games; the program does not contain them). Continue without them?
backport.fakelibEmpty: The fakelib folder was not found or is empty.
backport.mode.fself: Fake-sign only, SDK unchanged (dump from a console of the same firmware)
backport.outOptional: may be left empty — then the files are signed in place
backport.needFself: tools\fself\fself-cli.exe was not found. Rebuild the project (build.bat) — its sources are inside the project (bundled\fself).
backport.inPlace: “Save to” is empty: files inside the game folder will be MODIFIED (ELF → fake-signed SELF). No backup is made. Continue?
backport.noSpace: A copy of the dump needs about %1 GB, the drive has %2 GB free. Free some space or leave “Save to” empty (sign in place).
pack.decrypted: The game root has a “decrypted” folder — Dump Runner puts the original decrypted files there. They are not needed in the image and will make it much bigger.
pack.decrypted.move: Move it next to the game and continue
pack.decrypted.moved: The folder was moved (not deleted) to: %1
fpkg.engine.sdk279.missing: tools\fpkg279\build-from-folder.ps1 was not found. This is an optional third-party kit: put its folder into third_party and rebuild, or place it manually under tools\fpkg279. It ships its own Sony Publishing Tools binaries, separate from the built-in engine's sony-sdk.
fpkg.engine.sdk279.folderOnly: This engine only builds from a game folder, not from an image. Switch the source to “Folder”.
fpkg.hint279: Only used with the “SDK 2.79 plaintext” engine. APP requires an exact 96-byte sce_sys\keystone file in the source folder. AC is add-on content: no keystone needed, an entitlement key is required instead.
fpkg.entitlementKey.bad: The entitlement key must be exactly 32 hexadecimal characters (16 bytes).
fpkg.size.estimate: Uncompressed size: %1 GiB (with a metadata allowance ≈ %2 GiB) → expected attributePub: %3.
fpkg.size.tooManyFiles: Note: more files than level 2 (patched SDK) allows — a different profile would be needed.
settings.ftpEnable: Automatically upload the finished file to the PS5 after packing/building
settings.ftpHint: Needs an FTP server on the console (for example etaHEN's built-in one — Toolbox → Services → FTP; its default port is 1337, but yours may differ — check your loader). The folder is created on the console automatically if it doesn't exist yet. Enabled by default: set it up once, and the file lands on the console after every pack/build.
pack.ftpUpload: Upload to PS5 over FTP after packing
pack.ftpUploadTip: Configured in Settings → “Auto-upload to PS5 over FTP”. Unavailable if no IP address is set there, or ftpupload-cli hasn't been built.
fpkg.ftpUpload: Upload to PS5 over FTP after building
